$comment: Mission 1.74.2. The operator approved dispatch of the second enquiry, by a DIFFERENT mechanism to a DIFFERENT kind of channel. The rules invert against Mission 1.74.1: there a public issue made BYTE_VERIFIED reachable and pinned every field of the action; here a manual mail send makes it unreachable and leaves the sender undetermined until the act.

approval.$comment: The approval names a document by its hash, recomputed rather than asserted.
approval.why: Mission 1.66. An approval flag written into the frozen packet would change the artifact the operator read, and the packet's own validator asserts that the packet records no approval. That field means THIS DOCUMENT RECORDS NO APPROVAL and never that no approval exists.

approved_action.$comment: Mission 1.65's envelope rule. The digest binds the ACTION and excludes itself, the execution status and the recorded date.
approved_action.approved_subject: Terms scope: HEAD measurements of publicly reachable third-party websites
approved_action.channel_match_basis: the packet's channel is PROVIDER_DESIGNATED_TERMS_CHANNEL and its recipient is the address the Terms themselves designate in section 16; the approved mechanism sends one manual email to that address, so the approved action is the action the packet describes
approved_action.why_the_sender_is_not_pinned: Mission 1.65 stated this cost in advance and it recurs here: under a manual mail send the sender genuinely is not determined until the send, so the hash pins three fields of four. Pinning the fourth would produce a different approval that SUPERSEDES this one rather than editing it.
approved_action.why_that_differs_from_mission_1_74_1: the R1 approval bound every field, because a public repository and a GitHub identity are determined before the act. An email channel is not. The difference is a property of the CHANNEL, and it is the same property that decides the verification ceiling below.

execution.$comment: An approval says an action MAY be performed. Only a performance says it WAS -- and here the repository cannot observe the performance at all.
execution.why_byte_verification_is_unreachable_her: Mission 1.66 established it: a manual outbound send happens in a mail client nothing in this repository can observe, so no guard can establish that the message left. Mission 1.74.1 escaped that ceiling because a public issue has a durable public URL. This channel has no such artifact, so the honest maximum is an attestation, and the record says that rather than implying an upgrade path that does not exist.
execution.upgrade_path: NONE for this channel. A future mission may only record OPERATOR_ATTESTED. Importing a sent-message artifact from the operator's own mailbox was considered and refused in Mission 1.66: it would replace an attestation with an inference and require an access nobody requested.
execution.reachable_only_through: an explicit operator attestation that the message was sent, plus the sending mailbox, which no frozen document contains. This repository cannot reach SENT by any other route.
execution.mail_connector_note: a connector present in the runtime is not channel authorisation. An automated send of identical text to the identical recipient would still be a DIFFERENT action, because the channel is one of the bound fields and the sender would be a mailbox the operator never named.

integrity_checks_frozen_before_any_send.$comment: Frozen now, which is the only time they mean anything. A sent message cannot be unsent, so a duplicate is REPORTED rather than tidied away.

scope.$comment: The second of two. The first has its own approval and is unaffected.
scope.and_that_is_not_one_approval_covering_bo: each names its own enquiry, its own mechanism and its own recipient, and each authorises exactly one act. Neither may be used to justify the other.
scope.$snapshot_note: Renamed in Mission 1.74.3 from r1_execution_state_unchanged. The value is unchanged and is what Mission 1.74.2 observed; the old name invited a live comparison, and a live comparison refused the transition the R1 approval was built to make.

recommended_next_action.$comment: Two acts now wait on a person, and neither belongs to this repository.
recommended_next_action.action: the operator sends one email to legal@globalping.io with the approved subject and the frozen body, and separately posts the R1 issue
